healthcareSystem: State-funded basic healthcare with growing private sector. Tourists pay out-of-pocket. Private clinics in Yerevan offer good quality care at affordable prices.
qualityNotes: Private hospitals in Yerevan offer good modern care with some English-speaking doctors. Public hospitals are adequate but less comfortable. Healthcare quality drops significantly outside Yerevan. Armenia has a strong tradition of medical education.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies (դեղատուն) generally open 9am-9pm. Some 24-hour pharmacies in Yerevan. Good availability in towns.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies are plentiful in Yerevan and major towns. Many medications available without prescription at low prices. Pharmacists may speak some English in Yerevan. Russian is widely understood.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement is relaxed. Many medications including antibiotics can be purchased OTC. Controlled substances (opioids, psychotropics) require prescriptions.

restrictedMeds.name: Opioid medications
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly controlled. Must carry doctor's documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: Strong stimulants
restrictedMeds.note: ADHD medications like Adderall are controlled. Carry documentation.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English for controlled medications. Original packaging with pharmacy labels is recommended. Russian translation helpful but not required.

travelInsurance.tips: Recommended for private hospital access and medical evacuation. Healthcare is affordable but evacuation from remote mountain areas can be expensive.

vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations. Ensure routine vaccinations are up to date.

waterNotes: Tap water in Yerevan is generally safe to drink as it comes from mountain springs. Water quality in other areas varies. Bottled water is cheap and widely available. Natural springs are common and usually safe.
foodSafetyTips: Armenian food is generally safe and freshly prepared. Barbecue (khorovats) and fresh bread (lavash) are staples. Dairy products are fresh and safe in restaurants. Street food is generally reliable in Yerevan.
medicalTourismNote: Armenia is an emerging medical tourism destination, especially for dental care and cosmetic procedures at very competitive prices.
metaDescription: Health guide for Armenia: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, water safety tips, and insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Armenia Medical Center (Armmed)
hospitals.notes: Modern private hospital. English-speaking staff. Popular with expats and tourists.

hospitals.name: Nairi Medical Center
hospitals.notes: Well-equipped private hospital. Emergency department. International-standard care.

hospitals.name: Erebuni Medical Center
hospitals.notes: Large multi-specialty hospital. Emergency services available 24/7.

hospitals.name: Gyumri Regional Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main hospital in Armenia's second largest city. Basic facilities. Russian spoken.

pharmacyPhrases.english: I need medicine for a headache

dentalCare.availability: Good dental care in Yerevan at very affordable prices. Limited options outside the capital.
dentalCare.costRange: $15-40 for consultation; $25-80 for fillings; $20-60 for extractions
dentalCare.notes: Yerevan has many modern dental clinics. Quality is good and prices are a fraction of Western costs. Some clinics cater to diaspora visitors.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Private dental clinics in Yerevan can usually accommodate emergencies the same day. Ask your hotel for a recommendation.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Limited but available in Yerevan through private practice.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are developing. English-speaking therapists can be found in Yerevan. Online therapy is a good alternative.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is limited. Yerevan has some ramps and accessible buildings but many areas have uneven sidewalks and stairs.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Major private hospitals in Yerevan are generally accessible. Older public facilities may lack proper accessibility features.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Yerevan metro has limited accessibility. Taxis are the most practical option. Few wheelchair-accessible vehicles available.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Yerevan's cascade area and Republic Square are relatively flat. The older parts of the city and Dilijan/Garni have steep terrain. Contact hotels in advance about accessibility.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Tests available at clinics and hospitals in Yerevan.
covidStatus.notes: Armenia has lifted all COVID-related entry restrictions.

insuranceClaimProcess: Private clinics provide receipts and medical documentation. Request English-language reports. Keep all receipts for insurance claims. Healthcare costs are generally low.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs at private or international facilities. Public-system rates can be much lower. Actual costs vary by city, facility, and exchange rate.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation insurance recommended for serious conditions. Yerevan hospitals handle most routine cases. Istanbul and Tbilisi are the nearest major medical hubs.
